cards.text: Habakkuk the prophet has been bringing hard questions to the LORD, and the LORD has been answering him (Habakkuk 1:2-2:20). Now he does something different. This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.

cards.question: Habakkuk starts by telling the LORD he has heard the report of Him. How do the LORD's deeds leave Habakkuk?
Habakkuk wants the LORD's great deeds to stay in the history books. True or false?
Habakkuk asks the LORD, even in His wrath, to remember ___.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns into a picture: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah.

cards.question: As God comes from Teman, how far does His glory reach?

cards.text: His radiance was like the sunlight, with rays flashing from His hand. Friend, I can't look at my own oven light too long, and that thing is forty watts on a good day.

cards.question: Habakkuk says God's power is hidden in His hand. True or false?

cards.text: Habakkuk keeps watching God come. And He doesn't travel alone.

cards.question: In Habakkuk's picture, what goes before God and follows in His steps?

cards.text: He stood and measured the earth, He looked, and He startled the nations. Just a LOOK, friend, and I've been staring down my oven timer for years without it flinching once.

cards.question: In this picture, the ancient mountains and the perpetual hills stay standing. True or false?
Mountains that seemed to last forever fall, but Habakkuk says God's ways are ___.

cards.text: Then the prophet says he saw the tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian, two peoples who lived in tents. The Midianites came from Midian, a son of Abraham (Genesis 25:1-2).

cards.question: What's happening at the tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian?

cards.text: Then Habakkuk asks the LORD some questions, because of COURSE he does: "Were You angry at the rivers, O LORD? Was Your wrath against the streams?" He even asks if the LORD raged against the sea when He rode on His horses and His chariots.
The LORD brandishes His bow, calls for many arrows, and splits the earth with rivers. Me? I brandish a rolling pin and the dough just sits there looking at me.

cards.question: When the mountains see the LORD, they stay calm. True or false?
Torrents of water sweep by, and Habakkuk pictures the deep like a person. What does the deep do?

cards.text: Even the sun and moon react, at the flash of the LORD's flying arrows and the brightness of His shining spear.

cards.question: At the flash of the LORD's arrows, the sun and moon race across the sky. True or false?

cards.text: Then the prophet says, "You marched across the earth with fury; You threshed the nations in wrath."

cards.question: All that marching has a purpose. Why does the LORD go forth?

cards.text: The LORD crushes the head of the house of the wicked and strips him from head to toe. Selah.

cards.question: When the wicked one's warriors storm out to scatter Habakkuk's people, what does the LORD pierce his head with?

answers.text: A smooth stone from a sling
A tent peg and a hammer

cards.question: Habakkuk says those warriors came out gloating, as though ready to secretly devour the strong. True or false?
Habakkuk's battle picture circles back to where his questions began. With His horses, the LORD tramples the ___.

cards.text: Habakkuk has heard all of it. Now he tells what it does to him, from the inside out.

cards.question: What happens inside Habakkuk when he hears it all?

cards.text: His lips quiver at the sound, decay enters his bones, and he trembles where he stands. I know that one, friend: years in a junk drawer, holding my breath every time it rattled open, mustache shaking like a leaf.

cards.question: Shaking or not, Habakkuk says he must wait patiently for the day of distress to come upon the ___.

cards.text: Then comes the big though: though the fig tree doesn't bud, no fruit is on the vines, the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food. That's opening the cookie box and finding nothing but crumbs.

cards.question: In Habakkuk's list, the crops fail but the sheep and cattle are still safe. True or false?
Empty fields and empty stalls. What does Habakkuk say he will do anyway?
Habakkuk says he will rejoice in the God of his ___.
Habakkuk says his strength comes from his own hard work. True or false?
GOD the Lord makes Habakkuk able to walk upon the heights. What animal's feet does He make Habakkuk's feet like?

cards.text: The prayer ends with a note for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments. This prayer was made to be SUNG, friend, so somebody tune up those strings.

findings.problem: The card calls Cushan and Midian 'two peoples who lived in tents.' Habakkuk 3:7 only names the tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian. It never says who Cushan is, and the card gives no reference for that claim. The card also says 'The Midianites came from Midian,' but the reference it gives, Genesis 25:1-2, only says Midian was a son of Abraham.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question covers two groups, the tents of Cushan and the curtains of Midian. The right answer, 'They're trembling in distress,' gives both groups both details. In Habakkuk 3:7 the tents of Cushan are in distress and the curtains of Midian are trembling. The text never says Cushan's tents tremble or that Midian's curtains are in distress.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The question types follow a pattern: MC, TF, FB, MC, TF, MC, TF, FB, MC. Multiple choice is followed by true or false three times out of four.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: The question types repeat in a fixed cycle: MC, FB, TF, MC, FB, TF, MC.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Habakkuk's main request in 3:2, 'Revive them in these years; make them known in these years,' is never told. The only card on it is a false statement about history books. Its answer tells the baker what Habakkuk doesn't want, not what he asks for.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 5 only says the sun and moon 'react.' Nothing earlier lets the baker reason about whether they race or stand still, so the answer comes down to luck. The answer False also never tells the baker the key detail that the sun and moon stood still (Habakkuk 3:11).

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Exult in the LORD,' is the only answer that names the LORD and the only one in Bible wording ('exult'). The wrong answers, 'Leave the land' and 'Mourn the lost harvest,' are plain wording.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'The God of his ___' asks the baker to guess the wording of the line. 'Fathers' fits just as naturally as 'salvation,' and nothing earlier lets the baker reason out which word the text uses.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The climax of the prayer, 'GOD the Lord is my strength' (Habakkuk 3:19), is never told. The only card on it is a false statement that his strength comes from his own hard work. The answer False doesn't tell the baker where Habakkuk says his strength comes from.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
